what_happened_next.text:
Apple grew to about five times its starting value, and Microsoft to almost four times. Nintendo nearly doubled, as did the US share basket. Bonds gained only a little. The five years included a pandemic and large changes in interest rates, none of which made prices move in a straight line.

The pandemic arrived during these five years. WHO described it as a pandemic in March 2020 and listed its first COVID-19 vaccine for emergency use that December. In 2022, the Fed began raising interest rates. That July, Webb’s first full set of scientific images offered striking new views of space.

These changes formed the setting for the returns, but there is no simple rule assigning each gain to one event. The companies and broad baskets experienced the same years differently. Nintendo’s strong gain did not match Apple’s, and cash followed another path entirely. A good result can still come second or third; coming first is not the only way an investment can grow.

reflection.what_people_were_focused_on: People watched interest rates, climate talks, new games and an approaching spacecraft flyby. Technology companies reported their results.
reflection.what_actually_mattered: A broad basket and individual companies had different outcomes. Even strong gains over five years included periods when prices fell.
reflection.what_faded_away: A holiday hit or one strong quarter could not settle the next five years. Good company news did not remove the risk of its shares.
reflection.what_nobody_knew: The pandemic was unknown. It is easier to explain the eventual winners after seeing the chart than to choose them beforehand.
